notes:
LENGTH (PRD 2 to 6 min vs measured 10 to 57 s): I read the PRD as a first clear with retries, not a clean run (feedback section 4). For slots 8 to 11 I lengthen the strict Normal exit about 1.3 to 2x (8: 18.2 -> 18-26 s, 9: 12.3 -> 20-28, 10: 18.1/28.9 -> 24-34, 11: 15.5 -> 24-32) with 3 to 5 decision pauses each (a watcher deciding, a robot passing, a dog waking), never with longer walks: level 9 loses its kitchen and level15 loses two rooms. With windows this tight a first clear should take 2 to 4 minutes, which is the PRD band. Longer clean runs would need holds above 6 s (breaks rule 3) or more floor (breaks the review's finding 1).
ROCKER EVIDENCE: the rock lesson can only bind with a watcher who sees a stop without caring where it is. Humans with memory punish any stop away from the spawn (audit in-place radius 0.3 m, docs/m6/levels.json, which also showed the dog making the rock bind at 14.2 s). Rocking-chair decoys are impossible: collider half 0.30 + body radius 0.36 - skin 0.02 = 0.64 m minimum centre distance, above the audit's 0.6 m explained radius. So the rebuilt level15 uses a napping dog. Recommended alternative for the synthesis: swap level15 and level12 (dog at slot 10, rocker at slot 12) so each level brings one new thing; my level15 design works unchanged in either slot (the hint is the same), and in slot 12 the robot could return as a combination.
ROBOT: kept only in level 9 (now on the player's lane). Level15 drops its robot so slot 9 and 10 do not share a threat; the review's 'hum as reward' for the rocker is dropped on purpose.
NEIGHBOUR AXES (body / threat / shape / exit / look): 7-8 share nothing but the general east exit; 8-9 share body (chair) and exit (SE/E); 9-10 share exit (E) and a linear shape (band / hall); 10-11 share nothing but the south-east bias; 11-12 to be checked by act2b (level 11 chair, Lea walker, corridor spine, SE, green). All pairs share at most two axes. Exit variety is weak in this group (all east or south-east); flipping a whole level costs a full rebuild of stations, so I leave direction variety to act 3 and to act2b.
DATA THE REVIEW GOT WRONG (verified): level 9's robot is required by the hum (27 samples), not 'neither blocks nor helps'; my fix keeps the hum and makes it shape the route instead. Level 11's Lea starts at station 3 in the chambre with the player, facing the wall for 14 s, which is why the route never waits. Level 8's second door is not scenery for the door lesson (the chambre has no exit without a leaf) but the corridor is never used. Level 10's Mamie sit station exists but never fires before the exit.
SLOT TABLE AND SAVES: new act-2a order = level8, level9, level15, level11. Level10 removed from levels.json, file kept. Records keyed by id: level15's old best times must be versioned or reset (code). Unlocking follows the previous slot, so won levels 11 to 14 lock until level15 is won (code: R13 unlock rule).
VERIFICATION PROTOCOL (all unaudited by me, no Unity run in this wave): for each level, audit Normal and Difficile; compute waiting share and pause count from the route (numbers.py); for level 8 also audit level8_viaA and level8_viaB variants by absolute path; for level15 confirm 'lecon rock ... la bascule est requise'. First knobs if a target fails: level 8 sofa dwell 12 and its head-260 hold; level 9 robot speed 0.5 and Claire's glance hold 2.0; level15 Rex sleep 3.5 / awake 1.8 and Mamie M0 dwell 3.5; level 11 Lea station 2 dwell 6 and station 0 glance hold 2.5.
CODE ASKS FROM THIS GROUP (smallest first): test updates for the reorder, cut and rebuilds; hint tokens (QW2); record versioning and the unlock rule (R13); hum radius floor disc (R7, needed by level 9); start on first input (QW4, all four levels have a forced spawn hold that the 5 s intro card currently eats); optional audit 'barred region' and careful-rock options.
